chunks: Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to, when he sent a commander of his upon a battalion, order him to fear Allah Mighty and Majestic in his own private conduct first, then regarding his companions generally. Then he would say: 'Attack in the Name of Allah and in the Way of Allah. Fight those who disbelieve in Allah, and do not be treacherous, do not commit excesses, do not mutilate, do not kill any child nor any monk in a mountain retreat, do not burn palm trees nor flood them with water, do not cut down a fruit-bearing tree, and do not burn down crops — for you do not know, perhaps you will be in need of them. And do not hamstring from among the livestock whose flesh may be eaten, except what is absolutely necessary for you to eat.

And when you encounter an enemy of the Muslims, call them to one of three things: if they respond to any one of them, then accept from them and restrain yourselves from them — call them to Islam; if they enter into it, accept it from them and restrain yourselves from them. And call them to emigration (hijra) after Islam; if they do that, then accept it from them and restrain yourselves from them. If they refuse to emigrate and choose to remain in their homelands and refuse to enter the abode of hijra, then they will be at the status of the Bedouin believers — upon them will apply what applies to the Bedouin Muslims, and they will have no share in the war booty (fay') nor in any distribution, unless they migrate in the Way of Allah.

If they refuse these two, then call them to pay the jizya (tribute) in submission and humiliation. If they pay the jizya, accept it from them and restrain yourself from them. If they refuse, then seek the help of Allah Mighty and Majestic against them and wage jihad against them for the sake of Allah as is His right. And when you besiege the people of a fortress and they request that they descend upon the judgment of Allah Mighty and Majestic, do not grant them that — instead, let them descend upon your judgment, then judge among them afterwards as you wish. For if you leave them upon the judgment of Allah, you will not know whether you are reaching the judgment of Allah regarding them or not. And when you besiege the people of a fortress and they request permission to descend under the responsibility (dhimma) of Allah and the responsibility of His Messenger, do not let them descend thus — instead, let them descend under your own responsibilities and the responsibilities of your fathers and your brothers. For if you fail your responsibilities and the responsibilities of your fathers and your brothers, that would be easier upon you on the Day of Resurrection than if you were to fail the responsibility of Allah and the responsibility of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.الذِّمَّة: A covenant of protection; a binding guarantee of security
key_terms.الْجِزْيَة: Jizya — the poll tax paid by non-Muslims under Muslim governance in lieu of military service
key_terms.الْفَيْء: War booty that comes without fighting; revenues from non-Muslim territories
key_terms.تَغُلُّوا: Excess/ghulul — misappropriation of war booty before distribution
key_terms.تَقْوَى: God-consciousness, fear and awareness of Allah
key_terms.سَرِيَّة: A battalion or military expedition dispatched by the Prophet
key_terms.شَاهِق: A high mountain peak; a remote mountain retreat
key_terms.مُتَبَتِّل: One who dedicates himself entirely to worship; a monk or religious recluse
key_terms.هِجْرَة: Emigration; specifically the migration to the abode of Islam

ai.seo_question: What were the Prophet Muhammad's rules of conduct for Islamic military commanders?
ai.summary: This extensive legal hadith transmits the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) comprehensive military ethics code as reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The instructions cover two domains: first, the prohibition of various war crimes (treachery, mutilation, killing non-combatants, destruction of property and agriculture); and second, a graduated three-stage protocol for engaging the enemy — inviting them to Islam, then to hijra (emigration to the Muslim state), and finally to payment of jizya. The hadith reflects the early Islamic military jurisprudence developed during the Medinan period, when these rules were formulated to govern the rapidly expanding Muslim state's relations with non-Muslim communities.
